messages:
sam: Heads-up — seeing a persistent uptick in fncall validation rejects on prod (~+18% last 6h). Most are classified as 'reject' and we fall back to degen automatically. Users see degraded outputs and cost is up.

mika: Where are you seeing this? dashboard filter?

sam: In the fncall validation dashboard (per-route rejects). Quick query I ran:
```sql
SELECT route, validation_reason, count(*)
FROM invoke_events
WHERE time > now() - interval '6 hours'
GROUP BY route, validation_reason
ORDER BY count DESC
```
Most rows are validation_reason = "schema.missing_field" and a few "tool.malformed_json".

alerts-bot: [ALERT] fncall-reject-rate > 10% on /v1/chat.invoke (eu-west) — 4267890123 — see /alerts/4267

chris: If the dashboard is surfacing this as hard rejects that trigger degen, we should consider temporary reclass to soft-fail for selected tooltypes. That would avoid immediate customer-facing degen and extra charge.

jordana: UX note: console currently labels these entries as "Rejected by schema" with a red badge. Customers read that as a model failure. Proposal: change copy to "Structured output mismatch — attempted reconciliation" + a detail flyout with the validation_reason and example payload.

anya: From telemetry side we need a concise taxonomy so billing/console/routing can all interpret the same signal. Proposed codes: ["schema.missing_field","schema.invalid_type","schema.extra_top_level","tool.malformed_json","decode.timeout"]. Add a `validation_label` and `validation_action` (reject|softfail|coerce) to invoke events.

mika: Example of adding field to telemetry (proto/json-ish):
```json
{"invoke_id":"...","validation_label":"schema.missing_field","validation_action":"softfail","attempted_correction":true}
```
This would allow the console to show which ones were auto-corrected.

chris: Rollout idea: canary the new label + softfail rule for 10% of traffic on non-SLA routes for 48h. Collect sample payloads and surface top 5 example failures in the console for each route.

sam: Also need to decide billing attribution. Right now fallback to degen consumes tokens on the fallback model and is billed normally. We should either: (A) not bill the request that failed validation, (B) bill but attribute to "fallback-charge", or (C) bill normally but emit a chargeback tag so Sales can handle disputes. Preference leaning to C with visibility first.

jordana: For console UX I'd like two states: "Completed with fallback (validation)" and "Failed (validation)". For the first we show what was corrected and link to the sample prompt + returned body. For the second we provide clear remediation steps.

anya: We should also add an aggregator metric: percent_auto_corrected and auto_correct_success_rate (so we can measure if our heuristics make things worse).

mika: To implement: 1) telemetry fields, 2) softfail policy toggle, 3) console microcopy + sample viewer, 4) billing tag. I can prototype the telemetry patch.

chris: I'll do the routing/policy change and canary flags. Need a small endpoint on the control plane to flip softfail per-route.

ops-bot: Created ticket INF-2416: "structured-validation-labels + softfail canary" and assigned to @mika + @chris. PR template: include sample payloads and updated metrics.

sam: Thanks. Quick decision: do we auto-enable softfail for toolhooks that are known to be flaky (webhook, email-parser)? Or keep manual opt-in?

jordana: Manual opt-in initially. We should not silently change semantics for customers until we have the console explanation.

anya: Agreed. Manual opt-in + canary. Also add a telemetry flag so we can backfill which customers opted in for charge reconciliation.

mika: I'll open a draft PR with the telemetry field and a small migration plan. Will add sample rate-limited payload capture (PII scrubbed) for the canary.

sam: SG. Let's sync for 30m to align on rollout steps and UX copy. @chris @jordana @anya @mika — ping if you can't make it.
